prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for targeted protein degradation: the PROTAC concept and the molecular-glue mechanism of cereblon

statement.case_for: My final position is unchanged in configuration: base editing for David Liu alone, and targeted protein degradation for Craig Crews and Hiroshi Handa, three names in all. Both meet my standard of a game-changer that has already had consequences. Base editing is a chemically conceived capability, a deaminase directed to a chosen base without a double-strand break, validated in many independent laboratories and already used in patients. Degradation is a new pharmacological principle: Crews established the bifunctional recruitment of a ubiquitin ligase to a target, and Handa's identification of cereblon explains how thalidomide-type molecular glues work, so together they cover the design concept and a mechanism that is already clinically established. Each part has a short, explainable citation and no part needs more than two names, which is why I keep the pair rather than a one-part prize that would force a longer list of names for one field.
statement.case_against: The reservations from round 1 stand. Base editing is about ten years old, clinical outcomes are still accumulating, and a Liu-only citation does not settle Kondo and Nishida's independent deaminase-fusion work, nor the experimental first demonstrations by Komor and Gaudelli. No bifunctional degrader appears to be approved, and a two-name degradation part leaves out Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray. The pairing is two chemical-biology achievements and offers no unifying theme, and it concentrates the prize in the biomedical interface while B039 has the more mature record. I accept these as real costs; I weigh them as acceptable rather than disqualifying.

responses.point: The chair's configuration pairs B039 (Buchwald, Hartwig) with Liu for base editing, and asks whether the 2010 prize leaves C-N coupling a distinct, unrecognised principle.
responses.response: I agree on Liu alone for base editing, which now has the same laureate in four of eight files. On C-N coupling I have thought again: the mechanism-guided ligand design is a distinct advance and the Buchwald-Hartwig pair is the tidiest attribution on the list. But my test is a completely new capability, and aryl amination is a better way of doing something chemists could already do by other routes. I hold it as my first alternative rather than a preferred part. If the committee decides it wants a core synthetic-method part, I would not object, and the chair's Kosugi chronology question should be settled from the primary dates before that.

responses.point: Andrei's file credits Liu alone for B062, while his opening proposal and round-1 response text favour Liu with Komor and Gaudelli; he stresses the unresolved Kondo and Nishida claim and says degradation is somewhat early.
responses.response: We now agree that the file and the prize are Liu alone, which I welcome. I still think Komor and Gaudelli did the experiments that established the two editor classes, and I said I would reconsider if base editing were the sole part. It is not, and with a second part the name budget forces a choice; I stay with Liu as the intellectual originator of both editors. On Kondo and Nishida, the dated primary evidence is that their deaminase-fusion work used a different, non-clinical-grade system and did not give the general C-to-T and A-to-G editor classes. I read that as a precursor and not an equal claim, but I flag it as the main open attribution risk. On degradation, I accept that approval of a PROTAC is still pending, but cereblon glues are already medicines.

responses.point: Daniel's sole prize is degradation with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and he would accept Ciulli in place of Deshaies; he lists B062 only as an alternative.
responses.response: I now drop Ciulli from my own set and agree that the more defensible pair for a two-part prize is Crews and Handa, since a third degradation name would cut base editing out. Of Deshaies and Ciulli, I recognise Deshaies's 2001 PROTAC paper as the conventional priority and Ciulli's structural work as what made degraders rational; I do not think either belongs on a two-name part. I would ask Daniel whether he would join a two-part prize with Liu, since he already ranks B062 as an alternative and your Crews, Handa pair is identical to mine.

responses.point: Peter argues C-N coupling is overdue and clean, and that base editing is partly protein engineering and genome biology, with the 2020 CRISPR prize overlapping.
responses.response: I accept the CRISPR overlap as a fair challenge, but I read base editing as different in kind, because the deaminase chemistry makes the base change itself and not a break and repair. On overdue versus new, we differ in philosophy, and I do not claim the factual question is settled. I note that you and I agree on Liu alone, so the real choice for the committee is the second part: B039 or B066. I weigh the molecular-glue medicines already in use above the completeness of the C-N coupling pair, but I would not call that a scientific refutation of your case.

responses.point: Emma ranks condensates first with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen and lipid nanoparticles second, and says the trio is the most natural.
responses.response: Condensates remain my third-ranked candidate and an alternative. The Hyman and Brangwynne trio is natural, but the contested physiology and the question of whether the chemical content is distinct from physical theory applied to a cell keep me from placing it ahead of base editing or degradation now. I would reconsider if the committee wants a physical-chemical part with a three-name set, and I am glad the chair has asked what independent confirmation would persuade further members.

uncertainties: Whether Kondo and Nishida's deaminase-fusion work should share credit with Liu for base editing, or is a precursor.
Whether degradation should be Crews and Handa, or include Deshaies or Ciulli, if the committee prefers a one-part prize.
Whether the committee will accept a two-part prize of two chemical-biology achievements, or prefers B039 as the second part.
Whether clinical maturity of both fields is sufficient, since no bifunctional degrader seems approved and base editing outcomes are early.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited candidate on the shortlist. My Warshel and EVB background and Uppsala ribosome connections touch none of them. As a computational chemist I may be partial to energy landscape theory (B015), which is not in my preferred configuration. No change from round 1.
